Dear Director Aris,

I am writing to you today on behalf of the Eastside Transit User Group to share our concerns about the recent changes to our neighborhood bus routes, particularly the cancellation of Express Route 88.

For the past three years, I have taken Route 88 every single morning from the Heights District to my office downtown. It was always quick, reliable, and took just about 35 minutes door-to-door. However, ever since the new Route 402 replaced it last Monday, my daily commute has turned into a major headache. Because the new bus loops all the way around the industrial park and makes several additional stops along the way, my travel time has more than doubled. I now spend over an hour and a half just trying to get to work each morning. Spending three hours on a bus every day is exhausting and takes away precious time from our families.

This issue is affecting many people in our community, not just me. The Eastside area has a lot of hospital workers, retail employees, and students who depend on public transit every single day to get where they need to go. Yesterday morning at the main stop on 5th Avenue, I saw a crowd of at least thirty frustrated people waiting in the rain. When the Route 402 bus finally showed up 15 minutes late, it was already packed to capacity, and only a few people were able to squeeze on board. The rest of us had to wait for the next bus, causing many workers to be late for their shifts.

While I understand that the city wanted to expand service to new streets, the current setup is clearly not working for daily commuters. We want to support public transit, but we need a service that is reliable and reasonably fast.

We would like to propose a simple solution. Could the Transit Authority consider bringing back Express Route 88 just during the busiest rush hours—specifically from 7:00 to 9:00 AM in the morning and 4:00 to 6:00 PM in the evening? Leaving Route 402 for mid-day trips while running the express bus during peak hours would easily solve the overcrowding and get everyone to work on time.

Thank you for taking the time to read our letter and consider our request. We look forward to hearing your thoughts and hope we can work together on a fix soon.

Sincerely,
Jonathan Miller
Eastside Transit User Group
